name: Valsartan
summary: An ARB with robust randomized evidence in heart failure (Val-HeFT, VALIANT) and post-MI care, plus strong hypertension and diabetic-nephropathy indications.
mechanism: Selectively blocks the AT1 angiotensin II receptor, reducing vasoconstriction, aldosterone secretion, and sympathetic activation.

dosing.adult: Hypertension: 80–160 mg once daily (up to 320 mg); heart failure: start 40 mg twice daily, titrate to 160 mg twice daily

safety.pregnancy: Contraindicated in second and third trimesters (fetotoxic)
warnings: Hyperkalemia, especially with ACE inhibitors or potassium-sparing agents
Rise in creatinine with renal impairment

indications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction
clinicalPearls: Val-HeFT and VALIANT established it as one of the few ARBs with a labeled heart-failure indication.
The 2018 nitrosamine-impurity recalls were a supply-chain issue, not a drug-effect issue — generic availability has since normalized.
good: Hypertension with coexisting HFrEF or post-MI left ventricular dysfunction.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references (Goodman & Gilman, Katzung, Lexicomp-level standard facts). Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
